source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), General Directorate of Agriculture / ASPIRE program - Technical Document: "Sweet Corn Cultivation Techniques Resilient to Climate Change" (បច្ចេកទេសដាំដាំណាំពោតផ្អែមធន់នឹងការប្រែប្រួលអាកាសធាតុ), 2018
text:
Weeding: clear weeds regularly while the corn plants are still young, because weeds compete with corn for nutrients and slow the corn's growth. Weed by hand or with a hoe rather than using herbicide, in order to protect the environment and avoid harming neighboring plots/neighbors.

Watering: water is a key factor that can strongly affect sweet corn yield. Irrigate using a drip or sprinkler watering system where possible; watering frequency should be adjusted according to the actual soil moisture conditions and the season.

Fertilizer schedule (timing, fertilizer type, amount, and placement):
- Base fertilizer, applied 15 days before planting: rotted/composted animal manure or compost, at about 2 kg per square meter of bed, spread in two furrows along the length of the bed, applied then covered with soil before bed-covering (mulching).
- 7-10 days before planting: fertilizer formula 20-20-15, at about 5 grams per hill, placed at the base of the planting spot.
- 7-10 days after planting: urea fertilizer (46-0-0), at about 1.5 kg per hill, buried 5-10 cm from the plant base (2 holes per plant).
- 28-30 days after planting: fertilizer formula 20-20-15, at about 5 kg per hill (as recorded in the source table, though this large jump in per-hill amount compared to the earlier 5 gram application is noted as stated in the document and not independently verified), placed 15-25 cm from the plant base (1 hole per hill).
- 48-50 days after planting: fertilizer formula 20-20-15 combined with 0-0-60 (potassium) fertilizer, at about 10 kg per hill, placed 15-25 cm from the plant base (1 hole per hill).

FLAGGED NOTE: the source table's per-hill fertilizer amount jumps from 5 grams (pre-planting application) to 5 kg and then 10 kg (post-planting applications) for the same 20-20-15 formula; this could reflect a genuine large increase in application rate as the plant matures, or could be a unit inconsistency (grams vs kilograms) in the original document — it is reported here exactly as stated in the source without correction.

Other crop care: hill up soil around the plant base to keep it moist and even. Perform the first soil-hilling/mounding 15 days after planting, and a second round of soil-hilling 30 days after planting. Water or let irrigation water in whenever the soil surface is observed starting to dry out.
